_about: Starter posts for the Village Board. An elder publishes them with the 'Publish starter posts' button on /village. Fixed ids: publishing twice never creates duplicates. Edit freely before publishing.

posts.title: LeetCode week
posts.body: One LeetCode problem a day, from easy to a little harder. Solve it in any language, then share your approach in the comments: how you thought about it, not just the code. Stuck? Ask in the comments and someone will help.

days.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock (one pass)

posts.title: Lead WhoYouKnow: find a friendly intro to any circle at aivancity
posts.body:
A directory where students list the circles they belong to (associations, sports, programs, internships, home countries…) so others can find someone to ask for an intro. Opt-in only: you can list yourself, never someone else, and remove yourself anytime.

First step (about 2 weeks): a one-page plan (what a profile contains, privacy rules, how a request works), then a small prototype. You lead it; others can join you.

posts.title: Lead BeautyOfStats: answer curious questions with real data
posts.body:
A small site where each question gets a short answer, one clear chart and its sources. Example: which countries do people from India most often emigrate to?

First step: pick 3 questions, find open datasets (Our World in Data, World Bank, UN, OECD, Eurostat), and publish the first answer. Every answer cites its sources and says what the data can't tell us.

posts.title: Make the first video for the Tech Club's YouTube channel
posts.body: A 2–4 minute video: what the club is, a Thursday session, the Mountain. Write a short script, film on a Thursday (phone footage is fine), edit, then hand it to an elder to upload. Ask people before filming them.

posts.title: Make three short TikToks for the Tech Club
posts.body: Three vertical clips of 15–45 seconds: a coding tip, "a Thursday at the Tech Club", and this week's challenge. Captions on, and only music you're allowed to use. An elder posts them from the club account. Ask people before filming them.

posts.title: Audit the Tech Club: what works, what doesn't
posts.body: Talk to 8–10 members and 3 people who stopped coming, read the feedback inbox with an elder, and write a one-page report: 3 things to keep, 3 to fix, 3 to try next. Shared with the council. Keep quotes anonymous.

posts.title: Add "Add to calendar" buttons to the schedule
posts.body: Each session on /schedule gets a button that downloads an .ics file, which Google, Apple and Outlook calendars all understand. A small JavaScript task in the club's repository; an elder reviews your pull request.

posts.title: Build the projector screen for Thursday check-in
posts.body: A page for organizers that shows the session's check-in code in huge letters with a countdown until it expires, made for the projector. A good first task with Firebase and the club's code.

posts.title: Review the club website and report 3 bugs
posts.body: Try the site on your phone and laptop (Mountain, Village, schedule, sign-in), read some of the code, and open 3 clear GitHub issues: what you did, what happened, what you expected. About an hour.

posts.title: Hacktoberfest: your first open-source contributions this October
posts.body: Every October, open-source projects label beginner-friendly issues for Hacktoberfest. Pick one, open a pull request, and once it's merged, submit it on the Mountain as an open-source proof: it earns points.
